request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 1 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means results are clear-cut and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means the top configs are too close to call or something looks off. (Independent run 1, no feature agent.)

concerns: Run 7 (LightGBM) has the best PR-AUC at 0.7477, but its margin over logistic run 6 (0.7137) is about 0.034. That is well under one fold SD (0.052 for logistic, 0.065 for LightGBM), so the simplicity rule favours logistic.
Fold SDs of 0.05-0.07 mean most configs are statistically indistinguishable. Per-fold paired differences are not available, so the ranking is fragile.
Logistic run 6 also has the highest precision@50 (0.792) and the highest ROC-AUC (0.9453). Its PR-AUC is lower than LightGBM's, which is consistent with a noisy comparison rather than a clear winner.

ROC-AUC around 0.94 across every model family, including a heavily regularised logistic, suggests the label is largely linearly recoverable from aggregate features. It may be derived from claim volume or rule-based, or the features may leak it. The PotentialFraud label is of unknown origin, so a high score may only reproduce that labelling process rather than find real fraud.
The size features appear to help (all vs no_size: LightGBM 0.7346-0.7477 vs 0.7142, logistic 0.7137 vs 0.6809). Size may proxy for provider volume, so the queue could simply surface large providers.

Class weighting and no imbalance handling gave mixed results. Logistic with class_weight and C=0.1 performed worse than unweighted C=1, so the gap may be driven by regularisation strength rather than weighting.
Precision@50 is measured on folds of roughly 1,000 providers, while the real queue is about 100 providers of the full set. Precision at the deployment queue size is therefore not directly validated.
The time window (Nov 2008 to Dec 2009) is short and no temporal holdout is reported. Stratified CV may overstate how well the model generalises to new periods.
